title: India warns AI-powered hackers targeting crypto exchanges at ‘machine speed’
summary: India’s cybersecurity agency says a threat actor is escalating an AI-assisted hacking campaign targeting crypto exchanges and other financial firms.
content: India's cybersecurity agency has issued a warning regarding an escalating threat campaign. Officials state that AI-powered hackers are targeting cryptocurrency exchanges and other financial institutions at unprecedented speeds. This sophisticated, machine-speed cyber activity poses a significant risk to the security of digital asset platforms and requires heightened vigilance from organizations across the financial sector.

title: NCR Atleos Corporation Reports Strong Third-Quarter Results
summary:
NCR Atleos Corporation, a leader in expanding self-service financial access for financial institutions, retailers and consumers, today reported third quarter 2026 results. Key highlights include:
Total revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was $3.2 billion, up 1% year-over-year.

Total revenue of $1.1 billion in Q3, down 2% year-over year, with 71% from recurring revenue streams.
Net income attributable to Atleos for the first nine months was $184 million, up 133% year-over-year; Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months was $667 million, up 12% year-over-year.

Net income attributable to Atleos in Q3 was $97 million, up 273% year-over-year; Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $241 million, up approximately 10% year-over-year.
Self-Service Banking revenue for the first nine months of 2026 increased 3% with Self-Service Banking Adjusted EBITDA growth of 8%.

Self-Service Banking revenue for Q3 declined 2% due to lower hardware volumes in certain markets partially offset by growth in Software and Services.
Self-Service Banking Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 increased 7% led by ATM as a Service (“ATMaaS”), Software and productivity initiatives, which more than offset higher memory and fuel costs.
Network revenue was flat for the first nine months of 2026 with Network Adjusted EBITDA growth of 6%.

Network revenue for Q3 declined 2%, driven by lower demand in crypto transactions.
Network Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 decreased 2% year-over-year, due to timing of other initiatives.
Atleos continues to make significant progress toward completing the pending transaction with The Brink’s Company. Regulatory approvals and integration planning are processing as planned and the transaction is on track to close in early January 2027.
Tim Oliver, Atleos’ Chief Executive Officer, said, “We continue to make meaningful progress on regulatory approval processes across the multiple jurisdictions, and have significantly advanced the integration planning activities for the pending combination of Atleos and The Brink’s Company. The transaction is now expected to close in early January 2027 and the integration planning efforts confirm the rationale for the merger. Bringing together these two great companies will expand financial access, provide innovative solutions to our customers, and offer exciting opportunities to our employees.
Atleos delivered strong third quarter profit growth and a very good first nine months of 2026 despite revenue challenges from the war in the Middle East and some customers delaying buying decisions in anticipation of the combined companies new solutions. In the first nine months, service and software business paced our growth and our productivity efforts more than offset fuel and memory costs and pushed profit margins higher. Our service-led growth initiatives and investment in product innovation are encouraging financial institutions and retailers to choose our differentiated and comprehensive offering to meet their evolving self-service needs,” Mr. Oliver concluded.
Andy Wamser, Chief Financial Officer, added, “As we close out the third quarter, our results continue to reflect disciplined execution against our internal plan. We have been able to deliver strong financial results with year-over-year Adjusted EBITDA and EPS growth of 10% and 24%, respectively. Our strong financial performance to date has driven higher free cash flow with no borrowings on our revolving credit facility and further reduction in net leverage. We remain focused on delivering stronger earnings and cash flow conversion as we close out the year, enabling further net leverage reduction ahead of the anticipated transaction.”
Key Financial Highlights
Q3 Total Revenue of $1.10 billion, a decrease of $22 million year-over-year; with 71% from recurring revenue streams.
Q3 Net Income Attributable to Atleos of $97 million, an increase of 273% year-over-year.
Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $241 million, an increase of 10% year-over-year.
Q3 Diluted Earnings per Share of $1.27, an increase of 274% from prior year Q3; Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Share of $1.35, an increase of 24% from prior year Q3.
Q3 Net Cash from operating activities of $198 million, Q3 Adjusted Free Cash Flow-unrestricted of $156 million.

title: Finalytics.ai Launches a Personalized Digital Experience for Travis Credit Union
summary:
Finalytics.ai, the behavioral intelligence and personalization platform for community banks and credit unions, today announced the launch of a personalized digital experience for Travis Credit Union, built around what each member is trying to accomplish. Whether someone is opening their first account, shopping for an auto loan or exploring ways to save, the credit union’s website now recognizes that need and responds to it, instead of showing every person the same page.
The change reflects a simple idea at the center of how Travis serves its 280,000 members: no two members are in the same place, and the credit union should meet each of them where they are. In a branch, a Travis team member listens first and then helps. The personalized experience brings that same approach online.
For members, the difference shows up in small, practical ways. A young adult researching their first credit card sees plain-language guidance on building credit rather than a wall of products. A family comparing auto loans sees the rate, the monthly payment and a clear path to pre-approval. Each person spends less time hunting and more time getting the thing done that brought them there.
“Our members know what it feels like to walk into a Travis branch and be recognized. We wanted the same thing online. Every member should feel that the experience was built for them, because it was. This is about listening to what each person needs and making it easier for them to reach their goals,” said Grant Karsas, Vice President, Digital Experience at Travis Credit Union.
Finalytics delivered the experience with its platform, which recognizes what a person is looking for from how they move through the credit union’s website, and adjusts the content, offers and next steps accordingly. Finalytics also supports the Travis team with the copy, offers and reporting behind the experience, and measures success in the outcomes that matter to members and the credit union: accounts opened and loans funded.
“Travis started from the member’s point of view and worked backward. The question was never what the technology could do, it was what a member standing in front of us would need, and how the website could answer that first. That is the right way to think about personalization, and the Travis team held us to it,” said Craig McLaughlin, Founder and CEO of Finalytics.ai.
The personalized experience is live now across Travis’s website, and the credit union will continue to refine it based on how members use it.
